Early Tesla Inc. and Space Exploration Technologies Corp. investor Steve Jurvetson is backing two former leaders who worked at Elon Musk's space company, aiming to solve AI's rising electricity demand with off-grid solar and battery systems for data centers.

Jurvetson Backs Solar Storage Cost Overhaul

Jurvetson, who continues to serve as a director for SpaceX, announced on Wednesday that venture firm DFJ Growth, an enterprise where he is a partner, is investing in a startup named Ambrosia Energy, founded by Ben Longmier and Sara Spangelo.

"The endgame for datacenter power is solar, but it's held back by storage and installation costs," Jurvetson wrote on X, saying Ambrosia targets electricity at about $100 per megawatt-hour, 99.9% availability and deployment within one year.

☀️ I brainstormed a tagline for our latest investment,
Ambrosia Energy: "Sweet, sweet nectar of the sun gods!"

The endgame for datacenter power is solar, but it's held back by storage and installation costs. Ambrosia is optimizing solar + storage as a service: $100/MWh at 99.9%… pic.twitter.com/Eb5yLTwAJj

— Steve Jurvetson (@FutureJurvetson) August 12, 2026

Ambrosia says it vertically integrates land acquisition, permitting, engineering, battery manufacturing and construction. Its system combines solar with 24-hour lithium-iron-phosphate battery storage, while a proprietary installation method is designed to deploy panels 12 times faster than conventional approaches.

Trending: Avoid the #1 Investing Mistake: How Your 'Safe' Holdings Could Be Costing You Big Time

Jurvetson argued that plunging panel and battery-cell prices have made hardware just 10% to 20% of overall system costs, leaving installation and development as the bigger targets for savings. Ambrosia aims to reverse that ratio by stripping out nonessential infrastructure.

SpaceX Veterans Target Rapid Energy Deployment

"A power plant should be able to be built at any scale in 12 months from contract signing to power on," Spangelo said.

The founders bring satellite-industry experience to that task. Spangelo and Longmier co-founded Swarm Technologies, which SpaceX acquired in 2021, before helping lead Starlink Mobile. Ambrosia says its West Texas pilot has operated continuously and that its next project targets 200 MW of solar capacity delivering 20 MW of continuous power.

特斯拉公司和太空探索技术公司的早期投资者史蒂夫·尤尔韦森 (Steve Jurvetson) 支持两位曾在埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 太空公司工作的前领导人，旨在通过数据中心的离网太阳能和电池系统来解决人工智能不断增长的电力需求。

Jurvetson 支持太阳能存储成本改革

继续担任 SpaceX 董事的 Jurvetson 周三宣布，他作为合伙人的风投公司 DFJ Growth 正在投资一家名为 Ambrosia Energy 的初创公司，该公司由 Ben Longmier 和 Sara Spangelo 创立。

Jurvetson 在 X 上写道：“数据中心电力的最终目标是太阳能，但它受到存储和安装成本的阻碍。”Ambrosia 的目标是每兆瓦时 100 美元左右的电力，一年内实现 99.9% 的可用性和部署。

☀️ 我集思广益地为我们最新的投资 Ambrosia Energy 设计了一个口号：“甜蜜、甜蜜的太阳神的甘露！”数据中心电力的最终目标是太阳能，但它受到存储和安装成本的阻碍。 Ambrosia 正在优化太阳能 + 存储即服务：100 美元/MWh，利用率为 99.9%…… pic.twitter.com/Eb5yLTwAJj — Steve Jurvetson (@FutureJurvetson) 2026 年 8 月 12 日

Ambrosia 表示，它垂直整合土地收购、许可、工程、电池制造和建设。 其系统将太阳能与 24 小时磷酸铁锂电池存储相结合，而专有的安装方法旨在以比传统方法快 12 倍的速度部署电池板。

趋势：避免第一大投资错误：你的“安全”持仓可能会让你付出巨大的代价

Jurvetson 认为，面板和电池价格的暴跌使得硬件仅占整个系统成本的 10% 到 20%，从而使安装和开发成为更大的节省目标。 Ambrosia 旨在通过拆除非必要的基础设施来扭转这一比例。

SpaceX 退伍军人的目标是快速能源部署

斯潘杰洛说：“从签订合同到通电，任何规模的发电厂都应该能够在 12 个月内建成。”

创始人为这项任务带来了卫星行业的经验。 Spangelo 和 Longmier 共同创立了 Swarm Technologies，该公司于 2021 年被 SpaceX 收购，之后帮助领导 Starlink Mobile。 Ambrosia 表示，其西德克萨斯试点项目已持续运行，其下一个项目的目标是 200 兆瓦的太阳能容量，提供 20 兆瓦的连续电力。
